Legal lead Omar needs the completion report by 8 a.m. the next day, the change ID is CHG-772, and the backup set is BK-11.

The voice search study is led by Marta, with Leo handling analysis.
There are 20 participants: 12 employees and 8 customers.
The study runs from December 1 through December 19, 2026, every Tuesday and Thursday for 35 minutes per session.
The test items are:
• recognition at 65 dB
• correction of homophones
• searches longer than 20 words
• operation while wearing gloves
The task ID is UX-440.
We will use 6 Pixel 9 devices and 6 iPhone 17 devices.
The success threshold is a 90 percent search completion rate.
We decided to conduct half the sessions in person in room H-3 instead of doing all of them remotely.
The reason is that device volume and speaking distance must stay controlled so we can distinguish recognition errors from missing audio.
The report is due December 22.
The cost ceiling is 640 thousand dollars.
Participant compensation is 300 dollars each.

The endpoint certificate renewal is owned by Nakamura, with Sofia as administrator, and starts at 6 a.m. on February 8, 2027. There are 1,450 target devices across Paris, Berlin, and Madrid. The rollout is a three-stage process:
1. A 50-device pilot that verifies signatures.
2. 300 devices.
3. The remaining 1,100 devices.

Certificate ID CERT-57 expires on February 7, 2030, using RSA 3072 together with ECDSA P-256. We roll back if the first stage fails on 1 percent or more, and we stop the second stage if any device takes more than 8 seconds. Instead of one Sunday-wide update, we selected a three-stage rollout because that limits disruption for 150 sales staff working on Saturday to 40 minutes. The service stays monitored for 48 hours afterward, audit records are retained for 180 days, and approval SEC-204 is required before the final stage.
